According to the US Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) guideline from 2021, colorectal cancer screening should begin at age 45 years and continue until 75 years of age. Screening options recommended by the USPSTF include colonoscopy every ten years, annual FIT testing, or stool DNA-FIT test performed every one to three years. This recommendation is relevant for average-risk adults.

Please note that this guideline may vary based on individual patient risk factors, and other organizations such as NICE (National Institute for Health and Care Excellence) provide different assessments. Always consult with a healthcare professional for personalized advice.

results.content: The USPSTF recommends screening for colorectal cancer in all adults aged 45 to 75 years. Screening options include colonoscopy every 10 years, annual FIT testing, or stool DNA-FIT every 1-3 years.

Red flags requiring urgent evaluation of low back pain include new bladder or bowel dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, progressive leg weakness (possible cauda equina syndrome), fever with back pain, or a history of cancer with new-onset back pain (possible metastasis).
